entries.definition: What gives a flying boat, or a seaplane on a single float, lateral stability while it is at rest on the water.
entries.name: Lateral stabilization at rest on the water
entries.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "float, inboard stabilizing", "float, outboard (or wing-tip) stabilizing", "float, stabilizing (or side)", "sponson" and "stabilizer, stub-wing"

values.definition: Stabilizing floats placed relatively far out from the main float or hull, usually at or very near the tip of the wing.
Stabilizing floats placed relatively close to the main float or hull.
Protuberances from the hull designed to increase the beam or give lateral stability at rest.
values.notes: A sponson is part of the hull and is not a float: the report defines a float as "a completely enclosed watertight structure attached to an aircraft". Whether 25.535, which is written for auxiliary floats, reaches a sponson is a question this corpus has not read an answer to, and the absence of `admits` here does not answer it.

values.definition: Projections from the side of the central hull of a flying boat intended to increase the buoyancy and stability of the boat while it is at rest and to increase the hydrodynamic lift during the take-off; an integral part of the hull, usually in the form of a stumpy airfoil or a stub wing.
values.notes: The report gives this its own entry beside "sponson" and does not say how the two differ. Both are part of the hull; this one is also said to lift. They are kept as two values because the source has two words.

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934). The float entries, report page 15, read on the page image; "sponson" and "stabilizer, stub-wing" from the text layer, where they extracted cleanly. NTRS citation 20100021420.
verification.notes: The definition of the vocabulary itself is the report's "float, stabilizing (or side)": "intended to provide lateral stability while the seaplane or flying boat is at rest on the water". That `admits` names deadrise-auxiliary-float is this corpus's join and not the report's: the parameter is the auxiliary float's, so it exists when there is one.

entries.definition: Whether the propeller or propellers are forward or aft of the main supporting surfaces.
entries.name: Propeller position relative to the wing
entries.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "airplane": pusher airplane, tractor airplane

values.definition: The propeller or propellers are forward of the main supporting surfaces.
The propeller or propellers are aft of the main supporting surfaces.

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934), the entries under "airplane", read from the text layer of the NTRS scan, citation 20100021420, where they extracted cleanly. Not checked on the page image.
verification.notes: The report defines the two of an AIRPLANE, by all its propellers. An aircraft with both has no word here, which is one reason the vocabulary is not exhaustive.

entries.definition: Where a monoplane's wing is located relative to the top and bottom of the fuselage.
entries.name: Wing position on the body
entries.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "monoplane": high-wing, low-wing, midwing and parasol monoplane

values.definition: The wing is located at, or near, the top of the fuselage.
The wing is located approximately midway between the top and bottom of the fuselage.
The wing is located at, or near, the bottom of the fuselage.
The wing is above the fuselage.
values.notes: Above it, not at its top: the wing is carried clear of the body. The report does not say by what.
